narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist Matthew: orderly, grave, a teacher's storyteller.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord ending the Sermon on the Mount: warnings and the two houses; earnest, weighty.

1.t: Judge not, that you may not be judged.

2.t: For with what judgment you judge, you shall be judged: and with what measure you mete, it shall be measured to you again.

3.t: And why seest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye; and seest not the beam that is in thy own eye?

4.t: Or how sayest thou to thy brother: Let me cast the mote out of thy eye; and behold a beam is in thy own eye?

5.t: Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thy own eye, and then shalt thou see to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.

6.t: Give not that which is holy to dogs; neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turning upon you, they tear you.

7.t: Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you.

8.t: For every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shall be opened.

9.t: Or what man is there among you, of whom if his son shall ask bread, will he reach him a stone?

10.t: Or if he shall ask him a fish, will he reach him a serpent?

11.t: If you then being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children: how much more will your Father who is in heaven, give good things to them that ask him?

12.t: All things therefore whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do you also to them. For this is the law and the prophets.

13.t: Enter ye in at the narrow gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way that leadeth to destruction, and many there are who go in thereat.

14.t: How narrow is the gate, and strait is the way that leadeth to life: and few there are that find it!

15.t: Beware of false prophets, who come to you in the clothing of sheep, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

16.t: By their fruits you shall know them. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

17.t: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit, and the evil tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

18.t: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can an evil tree bring forth good fruit.

19.t: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit, shall be cut down, and shall be cast into the fire.

20.t: Wherefore by their fruits you shall know them.

21.t: Not every one that saith to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven: but he that doth the will of my Father who is in heaven, he shall enter into the kingdom of heaven.

22.t: Many will say to me in that day: Lord, Lord, have not we prophesied in thy name, and cast out devils in thy name, and done many miracles in thy name?

23.t: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, you that work iniquity.

24.t: Every one therefore that heareth these my words, and doth them, shall be likened to a wise man that built his house upon a rock,

25.t: And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it fell not, for it was founded on a rock.

26.t: And every one that heareth these my words and doth them not, shall be like a foolish man that built his house upon the sand,

27.t: And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and they beat upon that house, and it fell, and great was the fall thereof.

28.t: And it came to pass when Jesus had fully ended these words, the people were in admiration at his doctrine.

29.t: For he was teaching them as one having power, and not as the scribes and Pharisees.
